sources_considered.why: Primary experiments testing coherence and generalization of learned world models.
Primary chess representation and intervention research; relevant but specialized.
The March 2025 version documents interpretable state-tracking mechanisms before the post.
The conference publication is later than the post; the pre-post preprint was used instead.

evidence_items.explanation: Tests in games, logic puzzles, and navigation find weaknesses missed by existing diagnostics. This supports concerns about robustness in the tested systems, but does not establish inability across LLMs.

The chess-trained language model has behaviorally relevant, interpretable board representations. Its specialized training limits its use as evidence about general-purpose LLMs, but it challenges an unrestricted claim that language modeling cannot produce world representations.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; Belinda Z. Li, Zifan Carl Guo, and Jacob Andreas
evidence_items.locator: Abstract, sentence following the description of permutation composition
evidence_items.explanation: The experiments identify interpretable mechanisms for tracking successive rearrangements in trained or fine-tuned transformers. This contradicts categorical inability, while the restricted task and differing robustness of the mechanisms leave broader adequacy unsettled.

unresolved_gaps: No supplied criterion establishes when a domain-specific representation becomes an adequate world model.
The studies do not jointly establish reliability, interpretability, and sustained updating across a representative set of general-purpose LLM uses.
The evidence does not provide a common measure for comparing world-model failures with reasoning failures.
